gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ to your advice — then I would not be in this mess.
gaps.hint: regret about the past, past perfect
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus the past perfect expresses regret about the past: had listened.

gaps.sentence: I wish the meeting ___ tomorrow; I would rather sleep in.
gaps.hint: a wish about a present arrangement
gaps.explanation: Wishes about present facts use 'were': were not.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ for your quick thinking, the fire would have spread.
gaps.hint: the fixed phrase if it had not been for
gaps.explanation: The fixed expression 'if it had not been for' takes the past perfect: had not been.

gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: If we ___ nearer the station, we would not need the car at all.
gaps.explanation: An unreal present situation takes the past simple in the if-clause: lived.

gaps.sentence: If this medicine ___ relief within an hour, call me back.
gaps.explanation: Conditional instructions use the present simple in the if-clause: does not bring.

gaps.sentence: Unless it ___ below five degrees tonight, the event will go ahead.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' clauses take the present simple even when referring to tonight: drops.
